<!-- pr-reviewer: f4c70ab7c5e70a853684242223a4e2a7817fe728 -->
**Needs changes before merge.** One blocker: after a plate edit, a jaw block can end up inside the stock and nothing reports it.

Reviewed only this PR's own commit (`f4c70ab7`) on top of #823's head `fb03891c`. The PR is stacked on #823, so the fixture-plate commits belong to that review.

### What looks good
- The jaw-block model is laid out clearly. The block law covers the slotted body properly: every bolt must stay inside the body at every slide (`modvise.rs`, `check`). The solid is watertight, and its exact bounds and volume are pinned for every preset, both sides, with and without a slide.
- `fit_pair` is exact. The quarter-turn axes are written as plain numbers, so there is no rounding error from trig. The adjustable block goes on the nearest hole whose gap to the stock is zero or more, and slides by that gap. The fixed face sits on the stock's near side and the adjustable face on its far side, held to 1e-6 at 0/90/180/270. Every cast is range-checked first.
- The envelope never covers less than the real block. It runs from the body's rear to the insert's face, from the plate top to the taller of body and jaw, across the wider of the two (`mesh.rs:70`). Bolts and pins must lie inside the body's footprint. The insert is centred by construction.
- `PlaceModVisePair` is one undo step and redo works. It uses two `InsertFixture`s seated by #823's own `seat`, so each block carries its place on the plate (a `PlateMount`), just like a fixture put there with `PlaceOnPlate`. Deleting the plate lets go of both blocks, and a plate `MoveFixture` carries both and runs the clash check on them. All of this runs through the existing code, and `mod_vise_plate.rs` pins it. The posting gate judges the blocks (`the_blocks_are_judged_by_the_posting_gate`).
- Every refusal happens when the command is created, and each one says what is wrong. The `mod_jaw` key loads leniently: an unreadable key or one that breaks the block law is dropped and logged, and the fixture keeps its steel and its place. No version bump is needed, because older builds ignore the key.
- The MCP tool calls the same command, and `slide` is not overridable from MCP. The UI tests are structural kittest tests. The presets are round figures of our own; I found no vendor names or vendor dimensions in the diff.
- There is no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in the new non-test code. The new modules carry provenance lines, the new files are under 400 lines, no PNGs changed, no process files changed, and `CHANGELOG.md` is untouched. The PR body has a `Changelog:` line and ends `Fixes #820`.

### Local results (PR head merged with `upstream/main`: clean merge, nothing conflicted)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| build `cargo test -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --no-run` | ok |
| app `mod_vise` | 5 passed |
| app `mod_vise_plate` | 4 passed |
| app `mcp_mod_vise` | 1 passed |
| app `fixture_plate` | 7 passed |
| app `fixture_plate_riders` | 5 passed |
| app `builtin_vise` | 9 passed |
| app `fixtures` | 14 passed |
| app `project_roundtrip` | 71 passed |
| app `commands_undo` | 32 passed |
| ui `--lib fixture` (CWD `crates/ui`) | 32 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
1. **A plate edit can leave a jaw block inside the stock, and nothing says so** (`crates/app/src/commands/fixture_plate.rs:161` `reseat`, called by `SetPlate::new` at `:189`).
   - `SetPlate` puts each block back on its named hole and keeps the adjustable block's fitted `slide` (decision note: "re-seats it at the named hole with its slide intact"). If the grid pitch changes, the hole moves but the slide doesn't, and the stock stays where it is.
   - I checked this with a local-only test (not pushed), using the `mod_vise_plate.rs` rig: 60 mm stock, the 770MX plate, the 1 in preset at C14, fit at I16 with a slide of 22.55.
     - `SetPlate` with `pitch_y - 2` is accepted. The adjustable face lands at y = 14 against the stock's far side at +30, so the jaw is **16 mm inside the stock**. `fixture_clash::after_fixture_move` does detect it ("the stock 'Stock' would sink into the fixture 'Mod vise adjustable 1 in grid 3/8-16' ..."), but `SetPlate` never calls it.
     - `pitch_y + 2` is also accepted. This time the fixed face lands at y = -26 against the near side at -30, so the fixed jaw is 4 mm inside the stock.
   - The posting gate would still refuse a toolpath that hits the steel, so this does not post wrong NC. But the setup is quietly left in a state no shop can build, and the jaws are no longer touching the stock as the fit promised.
   - **Fix:** in the re-seat, for a rider that carries a `mod_jaw`, refuse the edit by name when the re-seated block reaches into the stock, e.g. "plate edit moves 'Mod vise adjustable …' 16.000 mm into the stock - re-place the pair". The fit's own "reaches into the fixed jaw" refusal is the model to follow. Re-fitting the slide belongs to #832, so a refusal is enough here.
   - At the very least, surface the `fixture_clash` warnings for re-seated riders the way `MoveFixture` does for carried ones.
   - Pin it with a `SetPlate` pitch-change test in `mod_vise_plate.rs`.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- **Bolt heads.** Only the bolts' footprint inside the body is checked. A bolt head standing above `body_height` is not part of the envelope; that's fine for counterbored blocks. Consider one line in the decision note saying `body_height` must cover the bolt heads.
- **Status line units.** The status line `slid {:.3} mm` (`crates/ui/src/state_modvise.rs:71`) shows mm in an inch document.
- **File size.** `crates/ui/src/state.rs` grows by 18 lines on a file already about 4200 lines long. This is the existing pattern, so it is only noted.
- **Follow-ups the PR already names:** moving `mod_jaw` onto #830's `fixture_keys` reader, and updating the camcraft-mcp skill table at the next process sync.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 5920a084ad2c22220dd3924483680cbe5c1d833d -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (once its parent #823 is in). The blocker from the last review is fixed. I found no new blockers.

This is a delta review of `f4c70ab7..5920a084`, the one commit `fix(app): a plate edit never pushes a mod vise jaw into the stock`. The earlier review covered the rest of #820.

### What looks good
- **`SetPlate` now refuses a jaw pushed into the stock, and says which one.** `jaws_after_reseat` (`crates/app/src/commands/mod_vise.rs:113`) measures each re-seated block with `modvise::reach::face_gap`. It works in the block's own frame and uses the same stock box as the pair fit. The message names the block, its side and the depth. I re-ran my earlier probe and tried more edits, all with a local-only test that is not pushed:

  | Edit (rig: 60 mm stock, 770MX plate, fixed C14, adjustable I16) | Result |
  |---|---|
  | pitch Y -2 / +2 | refused: adjustable **16.000** mm / fixed **4.000** mm into the stock |
  | pitch Y -0.04 / +0.04 / -0.1 | refused at 0.320 / 0.080 / 0.800 mm. No small edit slips under the 0.05 mm tolerance, because the hole index multiplies the change. |
  | offset Y -2 / +2 | refused: adjustable / fixed 2.000 mm |
  | pitch X ±2, offset X ±2 (across the clamp) | accepted, no warning |
  | Pair turned 90 deg (fixed F20, adjustable H14): pitch X -2 / +2 / +0.1 | refused: fixed 38.000 / adjustable 26.000 / adjustable 1.300 mm. Pitch Y ±2 accepted. |
  | Plate shrunk so row I or column 16 is gone | refused: "there is no location I16 (rows A-H ...)" / "(... columns 1-15)" |
  | Plate moved +5 X, +3 Y (`MoveFixture` warns: fixed jaw 3 mm in), then pitch Y -2 / -0.5 | refused: adjustable 13.000 / 1.000 mm |
  | Same moved plate, pitch Y +0.5: the fixed jaw, already 3 mm in, goes deeper | refused: fixed **4.000** mm |
  | Same moved plate, pitch Y +0.01 (the fixed jaw stays about 3 mm in) | accepted. The warning names both the lifted adjustable jaw (3.080 mm off) and the fixed jaw sitting in the stock. |
- **The "already in the stock" exemption is not a loophole.** The condition is `after < -deep && after < before - deep`. Any edit that drives a face more than 0.05 mm deeper is refused, as the +0.5 row shows. An edit that leaves an existing intrusion as it was is not refused, but the `fixture_clash` warning still names it.
- **Every rider is clash-checked.** `reseat` already returns the nested riders through `mount::carry`. `SetPlate::new` (`crates/app/src/commands/fixture_plate.rs:197-199`) runs `after_fixture_move` on every move, and `after_fixture_shape` on the plate's new slab at its pose. The warnings come back as `SetPlate::warning`, and MCP `set_fixture_plate` returns them as `warning`.
- **`MoveFixture` is unchanged by the split.** `after_fixture_move` (`crates/app/src/fixture_clash.rs:135`) now only looks up the fixture's own facets and passes them to `after_fixture_shape`. The `None` cases (unknown fixture, no facets) are the same as before.
- **Undo and redo are exact, and a refused edit changes nothing.** All checks run in `new`, before the `UpdateModel` is built. `a_plate_edit_that_keeps_the_jaws_clear_is_accepted_and_undoes_exactly` and `an_edited_plates_riders_are_clash_checked_where_they_land` pin both, to the bit.
- **The status line shows the slide in document units** (`crates/ui/src/state_modvise.rs:75`), and a new inch-document test pins it.
- The decision note records what was dropped and why: re-fitting the slide stays in #832, and an intrusion that existed before the edit is warned, not refused. It also adds the `body_height` / bolt-head line.
- Laws:
  - There is no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in the new non-test code.
  - The new `modvise/reach.rs` (49 lines) has a provenance line, and every touched file stays under 400 lines.
  - No snapshot PNGs, process files, goldens or `CHANGELOG.md` are touched.

### Local results (PR head merged with upstream `main`: clean, no conflicts; macOS, private target dir)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| build `cargo test -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --no-run` | ok |
| app `mod_vise` | 5 passed |
| app `mod_vise_plate` | 6 passed |
| app `mcp_mod_vise` | 1 passed |
| app `fixture_plate` | 7 passed |
| app `fixture_plate_riders` | 6 passed |
| app `fixture_plate_detect` | 3 passed |
| app `mcp_plate` | 1 passed |
| app `commands_undo` | 32 passed |
| app `fixtures` | 14 passed |
| ui `--lib fixture` (CWD `crates/ui`) | 33 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. **No jaw check when the stock was not in front of the block before the edit** (`crates/app/src/commands/mod_vise.rs:120`). The `let (Some(before), Some(after)) ... else { continue }` skips a block when `face_gap` returns `None` for the old pose.
   - Probe: move the stock 130 mm along X with `SetStock`, so the jaws no longer face it. Then make one edit with pitch X + 10 and pitch Y - 2. That carries the pair back around the stock with the adjustable jaw 16 mm in. The edit is accepted, and only the `fixture_clash` warning names it ("the stock 'Stock' would sink into the fixture 'Mod vise adjustable ...'").
   - It is contrived (the pair was already off its stock), it is warned by name, and the posting gate still judges the steel. So it is not a blocker.
   - A one-line hardening, here or in #832: treat a `None` before as "clear", so `after < -deep` alone refuses.
2. **The MCP `warning` field has no test.** `set_fixture_plate` returns it, but `mcp_plate.rs` does not assert it; the command-level tests do. One assert in `mcp_plate` would pin it.
3. **The UI has no plate-edit path today.** `SetPlate` is reached only through MCP: `state_plate.rs` covers insert, place and detect. So there is nothing for the UI to show yet. Whoever adds a plate-edit UI should route `SetPlate::warning` through `with_warning`, as `MoveFixture` does at `crates/ui/src/state.rs:3388`.
4. Carried over: `crates/ui/src/state.rs` is about 4200 lines (the existing pattern).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 0c529ac76c5d5191db1e44d8ca5c7cce84d5a867 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** This is a delta review of 5920a084..0c529ac7. The last clean review was at 5920a084. The only new commit on this branch is the merge 0c529ac7, which brings in #823's re-merged branch (4bb54336, already reviewed clean). The head already contains current upstream main, so the trial merge reported "Already up to date".

### What looks good
- `project/fixture_keys.rs::fixture_def` reads each key exactly once: vise, accessory, plate and on_plate (via `plate_dto::link_from`), and mod_jaw (via `modvise_dto::params_from`). None of them is lost, and `FixtureDef` is built with all six fields.
- The `mod_jaw` read is still lenient. An unreadable key and a law-breaking key are each dropped and logged on their own, and the fixture, its plate place and its steel all stay. The test `mod_vise_plate::a_pair_survives_a_save_and_unreadable_keys_are_dropped` pins this with a `"side": "telescopic"` shape and with `body_length: -1`.
- The "keep both sides" spots are all right:
  - `mod_jaw` sits beside `accessory`/`plate` in `FixtureDef` (schema.rs), `FixtureDto` (entity.rs), `wire::collect`, `TagFixture`, `ImportFixture` and `InsertFixture` (`with_mod_jaw`, `with_mount` and `with_accessory` are all kept).
  - The module lists in app lib.rs, project/mod.rs, mcp/mod.rs and egui_app/mod.rs carry both sides.
  - The MCP chain in `mcp/tools.rs` carries both `accessory_tools` and `modvise_tools`.
  - The `CommandKind` variants (`PlaceModVisePair` beside `AccessoryDialog`/`InsertAccessory`/`SetAccessory`) are both kept.
  - The draft retirers in `pages.rs` are both called.
- #833's safety laws still pass after the merge:
  - `a_plate_edit_that_pushes_a_jaw_into_the_stock_is_refused_by_name`
  - `an_edited_plates_riders_are_clash_checked_where_they_land` and `a_moved_plates_riders_are_clash_checked`
  - `a_pair_lands_on_the_grid_and_the_adjustable_jaw_touches_the_stock_at_every_quarter_turn` and `every_refusal_is_named`
  - `deleting_the_plate_lets_go_of_both_blocks`
- The merge touches no build.rs, `.github/`, scripts, xtask, Cargo files, goldens or snapshot PNGs.

### Local results (head 0c529ac7, macOS, debug)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| build `-p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --no-run` | ok |
| app `mod_vise` | 5 passed |
| app `mod_vise_plate` | 6 passed |
| app `mcp_mod_vise` | 1 passed |
| app `fixture_plate` | 7 passed |
| app `fixture_plate_riders` | 6 passed |
| app `fixture_keys_lenient` | 3 passed |
| app `fixtures` | 14 passed |
| app `project_roundtrip` | 71 passed |
| app `commands_undo` | 32 passed |
| ui `--lib fixture` (CWD crates/ui) | 40 passed |
| clippy `-p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. In `crates/app/src/project/modvise_dto.rs:24-39`, a dropped `mod_jaw` key is only logged with `tracing::warn!`. A dropped `vise` or `accessory` key also goes into the load notes the user sees (#812). This is the same as #819's plate keys today, so it is fine for this PR. A follow-up could pass `notes` into `params_from` and `link_from`, so that every dropped fixture key reaches the user the same way.
2. The module doc at `modvise_dto.rs:9` still says "When #830's shared `fixture_keys` reader lands, this moves onto it". That reader has now landed and is the caller. The doc line could be updated in that follow-up.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
